CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Sarah is a 27-year-old female presenting for her annual visit. She reports she has been doing better overall but has been struggling with depression off and on over the past year, particularly due to being confined indoors and working remotely. She is currently taking Prozac 20 mg daily, which has helped her in the past, and she feels that increasing the dose might help her through this difficult period. She also reports chronic back pain that is managed but bothersome, particularly when sitting for long periods at her desk at work. Symptoms improve with movement and position changes. She endorses some numbness in her legs that feels like the leg is "falling asleep" but denies tingling, pain down the legs, or weakness. The numbness improves with standing or changing position. She is able to perform activities of daily living but notes that both prolonged sitting and prolonged standing on her feet bother her. She has a history of congenital coronary artery disease for which she underwent coronary artery bypass grafting at a young age. She reports her heart has been doing well and her arteries have been looking good.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies tingling or pain radiating down legs. Denies leg weakness. Denies appearing in distress.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression, chronic back pain, congenital coronary artery disease s/p coronary artery bypass grafting

MEDICATIONS
Prozac 20 mg daily, Aspirin

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works at a desk. Has been working remotely over the past year.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: No apparent distress
Neck: No thyroid enlargement
Cardiovascular: 3/6 systolic ejection murmur, stable
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally
Abdomen: Soft
Back: Pain to palpation of lumbar spine, decreased flexion
Extremities: Good lower extremity strength, no edema

RESULTS
EKG: Basically unchanged from last year
Lumbar spine X-ray: Stable from last year

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Depression: Increase Prozac from 20 mg to 40 mg once daily. Prescription to be sent to pharmacy.
2. Chronic back pain: Refer to physical therapy. No pain medication needed at this time.
3. Coronary artery disease s/p CABG: Order echocardiogram. Continue Aspirin 81 mg daily.
4. Nurse to help schedule echocardiogram and physical therapy referral.
